overview: City Council President Nicole Morell discussed her path to local office, her role in managing council proceedings, and the current status of several major ordinances related to gender equity, surveillance technology, and affordable housing.

items.title: Motivation and Background
items.summary: Council President Nicole Morell shared her background in a civically engaged household and her motivation to provide better representation for resident views on the council.

items.title: Candidate Resources and Campaigning
items.summary: Morell discussed resources for potential candidates, including ward committees, city boards, and training programs like Emerge, while acknowledging the privilege of time required to campaign.

items.title: Gender Equity Ordinance
items.summary: Morell explained that the proposed Gender Equity Ordinance remains pending as the city seeks a permanent solicitor to refine the commission's scope and legal authority.

items.title: Responsibilities of the Council President
items.summary: The Council President described her duties in chairing meetings, managing decorum, and setting the legislative calendar for the body.

items.title: Housing Stability and Surveillance Ordinances
items.summary: The council recently advanced the Housing Stability Notification Ordinance to assist renters and the Citizen Control Over Public Surveillance (CCOPS) Ordinance to regulate municipal use of surveillance technology.

items.title: Affordable Housing Trust
items.summary: Morell detailed the establishment of an Affordable Housing Trust intended to facilitate the financing and acquisition of green, resilient affordable housing using Community Preservation Act funds.

items.title: Civic Engagement and Council Authority
items.summary: Morell encouraged residents to engage with the council's core powers over zoning, the budget, and ordinances to ensure diverse voices are heard in city government.
